result_semantic_payload.summary: Three CRM orders are confirmed by the payment processor's settlement log via verbatim order-id linkage with matching amounts: (1) ORD-70231, buyer wangqiang, amount 20000 — confirmed by settlement entry "2024-06-01 settle order=ORD-70231 wallet=TXabc111 amount=20000 ok"; (2) ORD-70232, buyer zhaolei, amount 15000 — confirmed by "2024-06-01 settle order=ORD-70232 wallet=TXdef222 amount=15000 ok"; (3) ORD-70233, buyer sunli, amount 31500 — confirmed by "2024-06-02 settle order=ORD-70233 wallet=TXghi333 amount=31500 ok". The linkage mechanism is that the settlement log references CRM order IDs verbatim (as documented in /README.txt), and the amounts match exactly in all three cases. One settlement log entry must stay separate from CRM orders: the entry "2024-06-02 settle order=ORD-72033 wallet=TXjkl444 amount=9999 ok" references order ID ORD-72033, which does not exist in the CRM orders table (the CRM table contains ORD-70231, ORD-70232, ORD-70233, ORD-70234 only). Per the README's explicit rule, a settlement whose order ID does not exist in the CRM table cannot be treated as the same order. Additionally, CRM order ORD-70234 (buyer qianer, amount 8000, status cancelled) has no corresponding settlement entry in the payment processor's log — it is a cancelled order with no settlement confirmation.

claim_candidates.text: CRM order ORD-70231 (buyer wangqiang, amount 20000, status paid) is confirmed by the payment processor's settlement log entry dated 2024-06-01 (order=ORD-70231, wallet=TXabc111, amount=20000, status ok). The linkage is verbatim order-id match with exact amount agreement.

CRM order ORD-70232 (buyer zhaolei, amount 15000, status paid) is confirmed by the payment processor's settlement log entry dated 2024-06-01 (order=ORD-70232, wallet=TXdef222, amount=15000, status ok). The linkage is verbatim order-id match with exact amount agreement.

CRM order ORD-70233 (buyer sunli, amount 31500, status paid) is confirmed by the payment processor's settlement log entry dated 2024-06-02 (order=ORD-70233, wallet=TXghi333, amount=31500, status ok). The linkage is verbatim order-id match with exact amount agreement.

Settlement log entry '2024-06-02 settle order=ORD-72033 wallet=TXjkl444 amount=9999 ok' must stay separate from CRM orders because order ID ORD-72033 does not exist in the CRM orders table. The CRM table contains only ORD-70231, ORD-70232, ORD-70233, and ORD-70234. Per the README rule, a settlement whose order ID does not exist in the CRM table cannot be treated as the same order.

CRM order ORD-70234 (buyer qianer, amount 8000, status cancelled) has no corresponding settlement entry in the payment processor's settlement log. It is a cancelled order with no settlement confirmation.

The linkage mechanism between CRM orders and settlement log entries is verbatim order-id reference: the settlement log uses the same order_id values as the CRM orders table, as documented in /README.txt which states 'Settlements reference CRM order ids verbatim.'

limitations: No timeline events were available for temporal correlation; all three files share the same mtime (1790594136) and no event-level timeline data exists.
No prior secondary analyses or claims existed for these evidence items, so all findings are freshly derived.
The settlement log does not record currency; 'amount' values are assumed to be in the same unit (USDT) as the CRM 'amount_usdt' field based on field naming.
No wallet-to-buyer mapping exists outside the settlement log itself; wallet IDs (TXabc111, etc.) appear only in the settlement log, not in CRM data.
warnings: Settlement entry ORD-72033 (amount 9999, wallet TXjkl444) is an anomaly: its order ID closely resembles ORD-70233 (differing by one digit in the third-to-last position) but is a distinct ID with no CRM match. This should be investigated as a potential typo, duplicate, or fraudulent entry.
